candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (Lists and registers, supervision hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Top-level index of every list the Czech National Bank maintains as financial-market supervisor: banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, small-scale providers, agents, foreign notifications. It is the entry point that snowballs into all authoritative enumerations of CZ payment actors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML crawl of the index to detect new/renamed list types; feed discovered list URLs into JERRS collection.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search on regulator register terms
queries_used: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB JERRS – Seznam regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu (application)
candidates.why_relevant: The authoritative, continuously updated enumeration of every licensed bank, payment institution, e-money institution, small-scale payment service provider and small-scale e-money issuer in CZ, with exact scope of authorisation, dates of grant/suspension/withdrawal and status. This is the ground truth for counting and tracking payment actors.
candidates.access_status: open (session/parameterised application; deep links may expire)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer WS JERRS machine interface; otherwise scripted browsing of the JERRS list-by-type views with a session-aware fetcher, snapshotting monthly for delta detection.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs search result plus snowball from ČNB lists hub
queries_used: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů platební instituce registr
candidates.observed_blocker: Application uses generated URLs; a plain fetch of a deep link may return an error page — unverified, not evidence the register is down.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Webové služby WS JERRS (machine-readable register API)
candidates.why_relevant: Official XML web services (live since 1.7.2019) exposing JERRS data: entity detail, list of entities of a chosen type (e.g. all payment institutions), and list of agents. This is the sustainable long-term collection channel for the CZ payment-actor register rather than scraping.
candidates.access_status: restricted – requires commercial qualified certificate (eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or EU trust list CA) for authentication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Obtain a commercial certificate, then scheduled SOAP/XML calls to https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws for entity-type lists; store paged XML responses and diff monthly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs search snowballed from JERRS register
queries_used: JERRS webové služby ČNB WS JERRS export seznamu subjektů XML
candidates.observed_blocker: Documentation states commercial certificates are required for WS JERRS user authentication.

candidates.source_name: EBA Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2
candidates.why_relevant: EU-wide central register fed daily by national competent authorities (ČNB for CZ). Allows cross-checking the CZ population of PIs/EMIs, passporting into CZ from other member states, and comparing CZ against peer markets. Whole register is downloadable.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled download of the full register file, filter home country = CZ plus passported-in entities; diff snapshots to detect entries/exits.
queries_used: EBA PSD2 register Czech payment institutions list

candidates.source_name: EBA Credit institutions register
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative EEA list of authorised credit institutions including CRD credit institutions, EEA branches and non-EEA branches — the banking half of the CZ payment-actor universe, and the cleanest way to track branch entries/exits into CZ.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled download; filter country=CZ; also mirrored as an open dataset on data.europa.eu.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en search, snowball from EBA registers hub
queries_used: EBA credit institutions register ESMA registers Czech Republic authorised institutions download

candidates.source_name: EBA – Registers and other lists of institutions (hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Index of all EBA registers (PSD2, credit institutions, crowdfunding, payment fraud-related lists); snowballs into further authoritative enumerations touching CZ payment actors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl to detect newly launched registers.
queries_used: EBA credit institutions register ESMA registers Czech Republic authorised institutions download

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Ostatní seznamy (other supervisory lists)
candidates.why_relevant: Holds the residual lists that do not fit the main JERRS presentation (e.g. notifications, special-regime entities). Useful for catching payment-adjacent actors that the headline registers omit.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly HTML crawl with change detection.
queries_used: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Číselníky, seznamy, registry platebního styku (bank codes / account code lists)
candidates.why_relevant: Official code lists for the CZ payment system — bank identification codes and related registers. A stable, machine-friendly key set for joining any payment-actor dataset (registers, statistics, terminal/ATM estates) on a canonical institution identifier.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the published code-list files on a monthly schedule; maintain as a dimension table.
queries_used: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznamy institucí pro potřeby měnové a finanční statistiky
candidates.why_relevant: The MFI-style institution lists used as the reporting population behind ČNB monetary and financial statistics. Bridges the licence register to the statistical universe, so headline payment/card statistics can be attributed to named institutions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic download of published list files; join to JERRS by IČO.
queries_used: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Pravomocná rozhodnutí (final supervisory/sanction decisions)
candidates.why_relevant: Full-text final enforcement decisions against banks, payment institutions and small-scale providers. Adversarial disclosure: decisions frequently quantify transaction volumes, fee practices, client counts and operational failures that institutions never publish voluntarily.
candidates.access_status: open, filterable by proceeding type, PDFs attached
candidates.legal_status: published by statutory duty (e.g. §14(1) Act 15/1998 Sb.)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the post-1.1.2009 decision list with the druh_rizeni filter, follow detail pages, download attached PDFs, extract entity + sanction + factual findings.
queries_used: ČNB sankční rozhodnutí správní řízení dohled seznam pravomocných rozhodnutí

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Zprávy o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem (annual supervision reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual supervisory report series (available back to ~2010) with counts of licences granted/withdrawn, sanctions imposed, sector composition and regulatory changes — the narrative and quantitative complement to the raw registers, and the fastest way to reconstruct multi-year actor-population trends.
candidates.access_status: open, PDF, cs and en editions
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the full PDF back-series once, then annually; extract licensing/sanction tables.
queries_used: ČNB Zpráva o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem publikace

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Vybrané předpisy vztahující se k platebnímu styku (payments legal base)
candidates.why_relevant: Curated index of the CZ and EU legal instruments governing payments (zákon o platebním styku, IFR 2015/751, PSD2 implementation). Defines which categories of actor must exist and must be registered — the schema behind the registers, and a pointer into interchange-cap rules relevant to fee analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl for changes; use as a pointer to EUR-Lex instruments.
queries_used: ÚOHS rozhodnutí mezibankovní poplatky platební karty sbírka rozhodnutí

candidates.source_name: ÚOHS – Sbírky rozhodnutí (competition decision collections)
candidates.why_relevant: Searchable full-text collection of Czech competition-authority decisions, each linked to related decisions and court judgments and available as HTML plus original PDF. Antitrust files on interbank/ATM-withdrawal interchange, card scheme rules and acquiring expose fee levels and market shares through adversarial disclosure.
candidates.access_status: open, search form; exact collection URL path may differ from the one given
candidates.legal_status: public decisions of a state authority
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query the decision search form with cs keywords (mezibankovní poplatek, platební karty, bankomat, acquiring), harvest HTML+PDF, follow the related-decision graph into court rulings.
queries_used: ÚOHS rozhodnutí mezibankovní poplatky platební karty sbírka rozhodnutí

candidates.source_name: ÚOHS – Platební styk (payments topic page)
candidates.why_relevant: The competition authority's dedicated payments landing page, describing its work on domestic multilateral interbank fees for ATM withdrawals and card scheme rules — the single best pointer into which ÚOHS case files touch payments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch and snowball every outbound case link; re-check semi-annually.
queries_used: ÚOHS rozhodnutí mezibankovní poplatky platební karty sbírka rozhodnutí

candidates.source_name: ÚOHS – Spojování soutěžitelů: oznámení o připravovaném spojení + merger decisions
candidates.why_relevant: Early-warning notices and subsequent merger decisions for banking, acquiring, ATM-operating and fintech transactions in CZ. Merger files routinely define relevant markets and disclose shares, branch and ATM counts that are otherwise unpublished.
candidates.access_status: open; listing URL pattern inferred from an observed item page
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the notification listing weekly, filter by NACE/keyword (banka, spořitelna, platební, karty, bankomat), then track the matching final decision in the Sbírka rozhodnutí.
queries_used: ÚOHS spojování soutěžitelů rozhodnutí akvizice banka platební služby bankomaty

candidates.source_name: ÚOHS – Tiskové zprávy, hospodářská soutěž (competition press releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Press releases summarise investigations before or instead of full decision publication, and occasionally reveal payment-market facts directly (e.g. an assessment of the bank 'vklad na kartu' cash-deposit-at-ATM service and ATM network expansion).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/HTML poll with cs keyword filter; link each release to the underlying case number.
queries_used: ÚOHS spojování soutěžitelů rozhodnutí akvizice banka platební služby bankomaty

candidates.source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Výroční zprávy (Financial Arbitrator annual reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory annual report (published by 30 June) with case counts broken down by product area, including payment services, cards and electronic money. Dispute volumes are a proxy for payment-channel usage and fraud pressure; reported caseload rose more than 4.5x since 2023 to 12,050 proceedings in 2025.
candidates.access_status: open, PDF series; site is present on both finarbitr.gov.cz and finarbitr.cz
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF download of the back-series; extract the per-product case tables into a time series.
queries_used: finanční arbitr ČR výroční zpráva platební styk spory

candidates.source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Sbírka rozhodnutí (published findings and decisions)
candidates.why_relevant: Anonymised full-text findings (nález), decisions on objections and resolutions, labelled by institution name and case number. Payment-services cases expose unauthorised-card-use, internet-banking transfer and fee practices at named CZ institutions — factual detail no bank publishes.
candidates.access_status: open; personal data redacted under §8a Act 106/1999 Sb. and §21(6) of the Financial Arbitrator Act
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the collection listing, download PDFs under /download/sbirka_dokument_cs/, index by institution and dispute type.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs search snowball from arbitrator site
queries_used: finanční arbitr sbírka rozhodnutí databáze nálezů platební služby

candidates.source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – Vývoj finančního trhu / Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu
candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance's annual state-of-the-market report (21 editions and counting) covering each financial-market sector, payments legislation and market infrastructure, with longer-term trend evaluation. It is the policy-owner's own framing of the CZ payments market and carries aggregate figures (e.g. CZK 12.2 trn in financial products in 2025).
candidates.access_status: open, PDF back-series; note the domain moved from mfcr.cz to mf.gov.cz
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the annual PDF each June; also monitor the ministry press-release feed for the accompanying data summary.
queries_used: Ministerstvo financí ČR Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu platební styk

candidates.source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – legislative materials on payments (důvodové zprávy, consultation papers)
candidates.why_relevant: Explanatory memoranda to payment-services bills contain regulatory impact assessments with counts of licensed entities, transaction and card volumes and cost estimates — quantitative market facts embedded in legislative drafting rather than in statistics releases.
candidates.access_status: open PDF; legacy mfcr.cz asset paths may redirect to mf.gov.cz
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Trigger-based collection whenever a payments bill is tabled; also cross-check the government legislative portal (ODok / PSP.cz) for the same documents.
queries_used: Ministerstvo financí ČR Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu platební styk

candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (Ministry of Justice) + ARES
candidates.why_relevant: Once a payment institution or e-money issuer is identified in JERRS by IČO, the public company register and its Sbírka listin yield audited financial statements, annual reports, ownership and statutory-body changes — the only routine way to size individually the non-bank CZ payment actors. ARES aggregates the same data plus the trade and VAT registers.
candidates.access_status: open, free; per-entity lookup by IČO, filings as scanned/native PDFs
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Take the IČO list from JERRS/EBA, query ARES for the structured record, then pull Sbírka listin filings annually; OCR older scanned statements.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs search, snowballed as the enrichment layer for register entities
queries_used: ARES obchodní rejstřík sbírka listin účetní závěrky platební instituce justice.cz

candidates.source_name: Portál gov.cz – Řešení spotřebitelských sporů u finančního arbitra (service description)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative statement of the financial arbitrator's jurisdictional scope (payment services, e-money, credit, FX exchange, etc.), which defines exactly which payment disputes end up in the arbitrator's published data and which do not — needed to interpret the caseload series correctly.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch; re-check on statutory amendment.
queries_used: finanční arbitr ČR výroční zpráva platební styk spory

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Regulations applicable to payments (EN mirror of the payments regulatory hub)
candidates.why_relevant: English mirror of the ČNB payments regulation section; useful for terminology mapping between the Czech statutory vocabulary and the EU/English terms used in EBA registers, and for briefing non-Czech readers without re-translating.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch for glossary construction; re-check annually.
queries_used: EBA PSD2 register Czech payment institutions list

negative_findings.description: No open, unauthenticated bulk download of the CZ licence register (JERRS) was found. The only documented machine interface, WS JERRS, requires a commercial qualified certificate from eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU trust-list CA.
negative_findings.result_summary: Machine access to the authoritative CZ register is gated behind certificate-based authentication; the EBA PSD2 register is the only free bulk substitute and covers PIs/EMIs only, not small-scale providers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Long-term automated tracking of the full CZ payment-actor population either needs a certificate procurement decision or must fall back to HTML scraping of JERRS.

negative_findings.description: No regulatory register in this cell enumerates ATM or POS terminal estates. Searches surfaced ATM facts only incidentally inside ÚOHS merger and press material (e.g. an ATM count for one banking group) and inside the ÚOHS interbank ATM-withdrawal fee file.
negative_findings.result_summary: ATM/POS counts are not a registered attribute in CZ; they appear only as adversarial disclosure in competition files or in statistical series outside this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ATM/POS estate data must be sourced from ČNB payment statistics or industry bodies, not from licence registers; the cell can only contribute episodic case-file evidence.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, permanently maintained ÚOHS index of interchange/card cases was found; the payments topic page and the general Sbírka rozhodnutí search form are the only routes, and the specific historical interbank ATM-fee decision was seen only via a summarised search result rather than a directly identified case URL.
negative_findings.result_summary: Interchange and ATM-fee cases must be retrieved by keyword query rather than from a stable curated list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must rely on repeated keyword querying and the related-decision link graph, with the risk of missing older or differently worded cases.

negative_findings.description: Two cell sources appear under two live domains each: the Ministry of Finance (mfcr.cz legacy assets vs mf.gov.cz current) and the Financial Arbitrator (finarbitr.cz vs finarbitr.gov.cz).
negative_findings.result_summary: Both domain variants returned results; which is canonical was not established and is not asserted here.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Stored URLs may silently rot or duplicate; the collector should canonicalise to the .gov.cz variants and keep the legacy domain as a fallback rather than treating a legacy 404 as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: The appellate layer over ÚOHS and ČNB decisions (Krajský soud v Brně, Nejvyšší správní soud judgment databases) was identified conceptually as the natural snowball target but was not searched within this run's budget.
negative_findings.result_summary: Court judgment databases remain an unexplored pointer source for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Judgments often restate the factual and economic findings of quashed or contested regulatory decisions, sometimes in more detail than the redacted originals.

coverage_gaps.description: Administrative court judgment databases (nssoud.cz for the Supreme Administrative Court, and the Krajský soud v Brně as the first-instance reviewer of ÚOHS decisions) were not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run cs queries such as 'NSS rozsudek mezibankovní poplatek platební karty ÚOHS' and 'krajský soud Brno rozsudek ÚOHS bankomat poplatek' and add the judgment databases as pointer/direct sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Passporting/notification records — EEA payment institutions and credit institutions notifying cross-border provision into CZ, and CZ entities notifying outward — were not individually located, though they are known to sit inside JERRS and the EBA registers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the JERRS entity types explicitly and identify the notification list URLs; cross-check against the EBA PSD2 register passporting fields.

coverage_gaps.description: Other CZ authorities with adjacent supervisory outputs were not covered: Česká obchodní inspekce (ČOI) for merchant-side conduct and surcharging, Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů (ÚOOÚ) for payment-data cases, and the Finanční analytický úřad (FAÚ) for AML measures against payment institutions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout ČOI, ÚOOÚ and FAÚ decision/annual-report pages in cs as an extension of this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB became supervisor for the crypto-asset sector under MiCA (noted in the 2025 supervision report), implying a new CZ register of crypto-asset service providers that was not located in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search cs for 'ČNB seznam poskytovatelů služeb souvisejících s kryptoaktivy MiCA registr' and add the register plus the ESMA MiCA register.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable; all were derived from search-result evidence. JERRS in particular uses generated, session-bound URLs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass, and for JERRS resolve a stable entry URL by navigating the application rather than by testing a deep link.

brief: The CZ regulatory-register landscape for payments is unusually well consolidated: the ČNB's JERRS application is the single authoritative enumeration of banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and small-scale providers, mirrored and cross-checkable against the EBA's PSD2 and credit-institution registers, with a documented but certificate-gated XML web service (WS JERRS) as the only official machine channel. The supervisory-output layer is rich and openly published — ČNB final sanction decisions with attached PDFs, annual supervision reports back to roughly 2010, and the Ministry of Finance's twenty-one-edition annual market report. The adversarial-disclosure layer is the highest-value and least tidy part: ÚOHS decision collections, merger notifications and press releases carry interbank ATM-withdrawal fee, card-scheme and ATM-network facts, and the Financial Arbitrator's published findings plus its annual reports quantify payment-services and card-fraud disputes at named institutions. Main weaknesses are the absence of any register-side ATM/POS estate data, the lack of a curated interchange case index, and dual live domains for the Ministry of Finance and the Arbitrator that require canonicalisation rather than dead-link conclusions.
